clue.text: He gave us Alastor

parts.note: points to the Russian composer whose symphonic poem took its name and subject from Shelley's poem Alastor

explanation.surface: A bare literary question about who supplied a particular work called Alastor.
explanation.walkthrough: Alastor reads as Shelley's poem, but the composer meant set it to music as a symphonic poem in 1913.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet composer wrote an orchestral tone poem named after Shelley's Alastor.

clue.text: Seemingly lofty, proud and arrogant -in defence of the Alamo, a brave man

indicators.note: a defence surrounds what it guards, so the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A heroic figure defending the Alamo is pictured as proud and haughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in defence of' signals letters held within 'Alamo, a brave'. The definition recalls Isaiah 16:6: 'We have heard of the pride of Moab; he is very proud'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the Moabite nation is condemned for its haughtiness and pride, so the kingdom stands for loftiness and arrogance.

clue.text: Novelist evokes expression of surprise

indicators.note: to evoke is to call up, here calling up the sound of the exclamation spoken

parts.note: 'Ah, gee!' is an exclamation of astonishment

explanation.surface: A writer is said to provoke amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: James Agee wrote A Death in the Family; 'Ah, gee!' spoken sounds like his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: James Agee was an American writer whose fiction won a Pulitzer Prize.

clue.text: Ruth Kahn (a CIA mystery) pupil of 1 Across

indicators.note: a mystery is something muddled and puzzling, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone called Ruth Kahn is caught up in an intelligence-agency puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mystery' tells you to rearrange RUTHKAHNACIA. Aram Khachaturian studied composition with Myaskovsky at the Moscow Conservatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The Armenian composer was taught by Myaskovsky, the composer who answers 1 Across.

clue.text: Latin man retains Russian agreement for Scandinavian leader

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: vir is the Latin word for a man
da is Russian for yes

explanation.surface: A man from Rome keeps a Russian assent in a contest for a Nordic chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retains' puts DA inside VIR. Vidar is one of the gods of Norse myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology this god avenges Odin at Ragnarok, a leading figure among the Scandinavian deities.

clue.text: Sound of noble Austen hero

indicators.note: the spoken sound of the next word is what is wanted, a homophone

parts.note: knightly means chivalrous and noble

explanation.surface: A Jane Austen hero is described as sounding noble.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Knightley is the hero of Austen's Emma.
explanation.definitionFit: George Knightley is the gentleman Emma Woodhouse marries in Austen's novel Emma.

clue.text: The present, as seen by Nabokov

definitions.text: The present, as seen by Nabokov

parts.words: The present, as seen by Nabokov
parts.note: a present is something given, and Nabokov's last Russian novel took such a word for its title

explanation.surface: How the novelist Nabokov regarded the here and now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The present' looks like the current time, but it is a gift; Nabokov's novel is The Gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is something given, and The Gift is the title of Nabokov's novel.

clue.text: A certain licence in publishing

parts.note: the official permission, granted by a church censor, that lets a book go to print

explanation.surface: A particular permit used in the book trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin term, meaning 'let it be printed', is the formal sanction that allows a book to be published.

clue.text: Hardy types test Haydn's composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are assembled in a new order

parts.note: the possessive S is kept as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A musical piece by Haydn is put to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' tells you to rearrange TESTHAYDNS. The Dynasts is Thomas Hardy's epic drama of the Napoleonic wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's verse drama about Napoleon is named for ruling houses, the kinds of people it portrays.

clue.text: A setting for Clea (and Cleo …)

parts.note: Clea is the last novel of Durrell's quartet set in this Egyptian city, and Cleopatra ruled from it

explanation.surface: A location for a novel, and for a famous queen too.
explanation.walkthrough: Clea is the fourth book of Lawrence Durrell's Alexandria Quartet; Cleo is Cleopatra, whose capital the city was.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian port is where Durrell's Clea takes place and was Cleopatra's royal seat.

clue.text: End of church seen in a pseudomartyr's memoirs

indicators.note: the answer can be seen inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Part of a church is mentioned in a false martyr's recollections.
explanation.walkthrough: Pseudo-Martyr is a prose work by John Donne, which helps the run look literary.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church is its apse.

clue.text: Conspirator offers brandy to American, fine champagne to you and me

parts.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape pressings
brut is very dry champagne
us means you and me

explanation.surface: A plotter hands out brandy to an American and good champagne to the rest of us.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcus Brutus is the assassin of Caesar in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: He plotted the murder of Julius Caesar.

clue.text: It would say little, indeed, for Lucy's —— or my Quakerism " (Bernard Barton, Letter 1837)

definitions.text: It would say little, indeed, for Lucy's —— or my Quakerism " (Bernard Barton, Letter 1837)

parts.words: It would say little, indeed, for Lucy's —— or my Quakerism " (Bernard Barton, Letter 1837)
parts.note: the gap is filled by a word for exaggerated attachment to church practice, set against the poet's own Quakerism

explanation.surface: A line from a letter by the Quaker poet Bernard Barton with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank: Barton contrasts Lucy's devotion to the established church with his own Quaker faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a churchgoing devotion to forms and ritual, the counterpart Barton sets against Quaker belief.

clue.text: The old man hobbles to set about getting secondhand document

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
limps means walks lamely

indicators.note: about means turned around or rearranged, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An elderly father limps off to get a used paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SET into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript scraped and written over again is reused, a document that has had a previous life.

clue.text: Four neatly realigned for Cedric Errol

indicators.note: realigned means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Four things are tidily rearranged for a boy named Cedric Errol.
explanation.walkthrough: Cedric Errol is the boy hero of Frances Hodgson Burnett's Little Lord Fauntleroy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedric Errol inherits the title Lord Fauntleroy in Burnett's novel.

clue.text: Symphony for a clergyman (and a neophyte)

parts.note: a pastor is a minister of religion
L, for learner, stands for a beginner

explanation.surface: A piece of music written for a minister and a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: A Pastoral Symphony is Vaughan Williams's third symphony; L is the learner sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaughan Williams gave his Symphony No 3 this title.

clue.text: Softly croons the —,

parts.note: the blank wants a piece of furniture that plays music, the combined wireless and record player of the mid-century home

explanation.surface: A line of verse about something singing quietly, with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A line of verse to complete: the thing crooning softly is the household radio-and-gramophone cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabinet combining a wireless and record player is the thing that softly croons music in the room.

clue.text: Blackmore's girl with connection to Welsh poets?

definitions.text: Blackmore's girl with connection to Welsh poets?

parts.words: Blackmore's girl with connection to Welsh poets?
parts.note: R D Blackmore's first novel is named for a heroine whose surname is shared with the Welsh poet Henry Vaughan

explanation.surface: Asks which of Blackmore's heroines is linked to poets from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Not Lorna Doone: Blackmore's first novel was Clara Vaughan, and Henry Vaughan was a Welsh metaphysical poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara Vaughan is the title heroine of Blackmore's first novel, sharing her surname with Henry Vaughan.

clue.text: Room for James Merrill

parts.note: Merrill's 1988 collection of poems is titled The ___ Room

explanation.surface: Asks for space to be made for the poet James Merrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room' reads as space, but completes the title of James Merrill's book The Inner Room.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inner Room is a 1988 volume by the American poet James Merrill.

clue.text: Dessicated doctor friend of Scott protagonist

definitions.meaning: dried out, as arid as powder
the Reverend Dr Jonas, the fictional antiquary to whom Scott addresses prefaces to his novels

explanation.surface: A dried-up physician who is a pal of a Walter Scott hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Jonas Dryasdust is the pedantic antiquary to whom Scott addresses the prefaces of Ivanhoe and other novels.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means utterly dry, and as a name it belongs to Scott's invented antiquarian correspondent.

clue.text: Tudor ballet a guide for desert wanderers 2,

definitions.meaning: Antony Tudor choreographed a 1942 ballet to Schoenberg's Verklärte Nacht under this title
in Exodus a blazing column led the Israelites through the wilderness by night

explanation.surface: A Tudor dance that serves to guide people lost in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tudor' is not the royal dynasty but the choreographer Antony Tudor.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Tudor's ballet is the biblical column of flame that led the Israelites at night.

clue.text: Dali's was visible

parts.note: Dali's 1930 book and image La ___ visible names a woman in French

explanation.surface: Something of Salvador Dali's could be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Dali published La Femme visible in 1930; 'femme' is French for woman.
explanation.definitionFit: La Femme visible is the title of Dali's 1930 work, and the French word means woman.

clue.text: Audibly eager actor

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: A keen performer speaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Kean was the great Shakespearean actor of the Regency stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Kean was a celebrated English tragedian, famous as Shylock and Richard III.

clue.text: Masonic river?

parts.note: the Egyptian goddess revered in Masonic symbolism shares her name with the Thames at Oxford

explanation.surface: Asks whether a watercourse belongs to the Freemasons.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thames is called by this name as it flows through Oxford; the goddess also figures in Masonic lore.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian goddess appears in Masonic ritual, and her name is given to the Thames at Oxford.

clue.text: A noble version of Lear

indicators.note: a version is another form of something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman as a retelling of King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges the letters of LEAR; Lear's play is full of earls.
explanation.definitionFit: This British peer ranks between marquess and viscount.

clue.text: Forethought secured by Aeschylus, liberated by Shelley

definitions.text: Forethought secured by Aeschylus, liberated by Shelley

parts.words: Forethought secured by Aeschylus, liberated by Shelley
parts.note: the Titan whose name means forethought is chained in Aeschylus's play and freed in Shelley's lyrical drama

explanation.surface: Prudent planning made safe by one writer and set loose by another.
explanation.walkthrough: Aeschylus wrote Prometheus Bound and Shelley Prometheus Unbound; the Greek name means forethought.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titan's Greek name means foresight, and he is bound by Aeschylus and unbound by Shelley.

clue.text: Saki gave us these postwar playthings

definitions.text: Saki gave us these postwar playthings

parts.words: Saki gave us these postwar playthings
parts.note: Saki's posthumous story collection is The ___ of Peace, playthings for after the fighting

explanation.surface: The writer Saki handed out games for after the war.
explanation.walkthrough: Saki's collection The Toys of Peace appeared in 1919.
explanation.definitionFit: Saki's book The Toys of Peace names playthings for a time after war.

clue.text: Signs of additions among these campers and sportsmen

indicators.note: the answer lies among the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Marks of addition turn up among holidaymakers and athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans 'campers and sportsmen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol & is the sign meaning 'and', used for adding things together.
